Exploring entanglement in high-energy particle collisions offers unique opportunities to probe quantum phenomena under extreme conditions. Here we demonstrate the observation of quantum entanglement between lambda and anti-lambda hyperons ($\Lambda\bar{\Lambda}$) produced in electron-positron collisions via the decay of the $J/\psi$ particle. By analyzing the angular correlations of the protons and antiprotons emerging from the subsequent weak decays of the hyperons, we identify clear signatures of entanglement that violate the limits derived for product states. This result confirms that entanglement persists through both the strong interaction production process and the weak decay processes. We further establish a general polar-azimuthal selection rule showing that azimuthal correlations are indispensable for entanglement certification in spin-$1/2$ fermion-antifermion systems. It is also confirmed that a significant majority of these decay events occur at spacelike separation, meaning that no classical signal could connect them. The successful detection of entanglement in this hyperon-antihyperon system establishes a new methodology and platform for measuring quantum properties in relativistic particle physics, complementing traditional approaches and opening avenues for future investigations into decoherence or symmetry violations in high-energy collisions.

hep-ph.title: Two-loop renormalisation of quark and gluon fields in the SMEFT in the on-shell scheme
hep-ph.author: Claude Duhr, Giuseppe Ventura, Eleni Vryonidou
hep-ph.abstract: We compute the contributions of CP-conserving dimension-six SMEFT operators to the two-loop renormalisation constants of quark and gluon fields in the on-shell scheme. Specifically, we consider the top-quark chromomagnetic operator and the triple gluon operator. We also compute the contribution of four-quark operators to the gluon renormalisation constant and discuss the implications for the running of the strong coupling constant.

hep-ph.title: Higgs Signal Strength Estimation with Machine Learning under Systematic Uncertainties
hep-ph.author: Minxuan He, Claudius Krause, Daohan Wang
hep-ph.abstract: We present a dedicated graph neural network (GNN)-based methodology for the extraction of the Higgs boson signal strength $\mu$, incorporating systematic uncertainties. The architecture features two branches: a deterministic GNN that processes kinematic variables unaffected by nuisance parameters, and an uncertainty-aware GNN that handles inputs modulated by systematic effects through gated attention-based message passing. Their outputs are fused to produce classification scores for signal-background discrimination. During training we sample nuisance-parameter configurations and aggregate the loss across them, promoting stability of the classifier under systematic shifts and effectively decorrelating its outputs from nuisance variations. The resulting binned classifier outputs are used to construct a Poisson likelihood, which enables profile likelihood scans over signal strength, with nuisance parameters profiled out via numerical optimization. We validate this framework on the FAIR Universe Higgs Uncertainty Challenge dataset, yielding accurate estimation of signal strength $\mu$ and its 68.27\% confidence interval, achieving competitive coverage and interval widths in large-scale pseudo-experiments. Our code "Systematics-Aware Graph Estimator" (SAGE) is publicly available.

hep-ph.title: Chiral spin symmetry
hep-ph.author: L. Ya. Glozman
hep-ph.abstract: We review the chiral spin symmetry, which is a symmetry of the color charge and of the confining electric part of QCD. Observation of this symmetry in the vacuum upon truncation of the near-zero modes of the Dirac operator implies that the hadron mass in the light quark sector is not due to the quark condensate of the vacuum and that confinement and chiral symmetry breaking are not directly related. Observation of this symmetry above the chiral symmetry restoration crossover suggests that QCD is still in the confining regime with chirally symmetric quarks bound into the color-singlets by the confining electric field. This regime of QCD was called a stringy fluid. At a temperature T_d that is essentially above T_ch the chiral spin symmetry smoothly disappears suggesting that the confining electric field gets screened and one observes a very smooth crossover to the quark-gluon plasma. The three-regimes picture has been further substantiated by the analysis of the N_c scaling of the energy density, the pressure and the entropy density. In the hadron gas they scale as N_c^0, in the stringy fluid as N_c^1 and in the quark-gluon plasma as N_c^2. We have analyzed the fluctuations of conserved charges that scale as N_c^1 above T_ch thus indicating a transition from the hadron gas to the stringy fluid. When N_c gets sufficiently large the three-regimes picture transforms into the three-phases phase diagram. Finally we discuss a confining and chirally symmetric model in 3+1 dimensions. This model demonstrates the chiral symmetry restoration in the confining regime and a delocalization of the color-singlet quark-antiquark systems that become very large at T > T_ch. Consequently the stringy fluid matter is a very dense highly collective system of the overlapping very large color-singlet quark-antiquark "mesons" with a very small mean free path.

hep-ph.title: Asymmetric Dark Matter from Low-Scale Spontaneous Leptogenesis
hep-ph.author: Hiroki Takahashi, Juntaro Wada
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate a novel type of asymmetric dark matter (ADM) model in which the dark matter asymmetry and the baryon asymmetry in our universe (BAU) are produced simultaneously via low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis, where the mass scale of right-handed neutrino is much lower than the Davidson-Ibarra bound $M_1 \ll 10^{9}~\rm{GeV}$. In our scenario, both asymmetries are predominantly sourced by a dynamical $CP$ phase, namely the majoron. Its kinetic misalignment provides a sufficiently large, time-dependent effective $CP$ phase, allowing efficient asymmetry production even for low-scale right-handed neutrinos. In our framework, the sources of $CP$ violation responsible for the BAU and ADM are correlated with each other, leading to a predictive relation for the dark matter mass. In particular, when the dark matter asymmetry reaches its equilibrium value before freeze-out, the dark matter mass is typically predicted to lie in the range $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_{\chi} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{GeV}$, which lies within the sensitivity of direct detection experiments. On the other hand, if the dark matter asymmetry does not reach its equilibrium value due to weak coupling, the allowed mass range extends over a broader interval, $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_{\chi} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10)~\rm{TeV}$.

hep-ph.title: Two-loop renormalisation of the quark fields in the presence of four-fermion SMEFT operators
hep-ph.author: Claude Duhr, Giuseppe Ventura, Eleni Vryonidou
hep-ph.abstract: We compute the contributions of the dimension-6 SMEFT operators involving four third-generation quarks to the two-loop renormalisation of the quark fields and masses. We perform the computations in both the Naive Dimensional Regularisation (NDR) and the Breitenlohner-Maison-`t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) schemes, and we present results for all relevant field and mass renormalisation constants in the on-shell and MS-bar schemes. We carefully discuss all scheme choices which affect the final results. This completes the computation of field and mass renormalisation constants relevant for two-loop computations in QCD involving dimension-six SMEFT operators.

hep-ph.title: Charmonium production at energies available at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron and Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research
hep-ph.author: Taesoo Song, Jiaxing Zhao, Joerg Aichelin, Elena Bratkovskaya
hep-ph.abstract: In this study we apply the Remler formalism to charmonium production at SPS and GSI/FAIR energies in order to investigate the effects of baryon-rich matter on charmonium production and dissociation in heavy-ion collisions within the Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD). As a first step the Remler formalism is tested in p+p collisions and then applied to p+A collisions in order to extract the nuclear absorption cross section of charmonium, which is then utilized in heavy-ion collisions. We find that the Remler formalism successfully describes charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies when an in-medium heavy quark potential is implemented, in which $J/\psi$ dissociates near $T_c$. Finally the same formalism is applied to the low CERN/SPS energy and GSI/FAIR energies, where we estimate charmonium production.

hep-ph.title: Probing TeV-scale Majorana neutrinos at a muon-proton collider via a lepton-number-violating fat-jet signature
hep-ph.author: Yao-Bei Liu
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity to TeV-scale heavy Majorana neutrinos at a future muon-proton collider with $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV, based on 1~TeV muon and 7~TeV proton beams. We focus on the lepton-number-violating (LNV) process $\mu^- p \to jN$, followed by $N\to\mu^+W^-\to\mu^+J$, leading to the characteristic final state $j\mu^+J$. Here, $j$ denotes the associated light jet from heavy-neutrino production, while $J$ denotes the fat jet originating from the hadronic decay of the highly boosted $W$ boson. This topology provides a clean experimental signature with strongly suppressed Standard Model backgrounds. A comprehensive signal and background analysis is performed using parton showering, fast detector simulation, and dedicated fat-jet reconstruction. We derive the projected $2\sigma$ exclusion limits on the muon-flavor mixing parameter $|V_{\mu N}|^2$ for integrated luminosities of $100$~fb$^{-1}$ and $1$~ab$^{-1}$. For heavy-neutrino masses in the range $1~\mathrm{TeV}\leq m_N\leq3~\mathrm{TeV}$, the projected upper limits on $|V_{\mu N}|^2$ range from $2.6\times10^{-6}$ to $5.9\times10^{-5}$ at $1$~ab$^{-1}$. These results show that a future $\mu p$ collider can provide competitive and complementary sensitivity to TeV-scale heavy Majorana neutrinos compared with other proposed high-energy facilities.

hep-ph.title: Renormalon subtracted nonrelativistic QCD for heavy hadron systems
hep-ph.author: Benoît Assi, Andreas S. Kronfeld, Simon Vaiva, Michael L. Wagman
hep-ph.abstract: We present a renormalon-subtracted formulation of potential nonrelativistic QCD (pNRQCD) for precision spectroscopy of heavy hadron systems, combining variational and Green's function Monte Carlo (VMC/GFMC) methods with static two- and three-body potentials through NNLO in $\alpha_s$ (leading order in $1/m_Q$). Minimal renormalon subtraction (MRS) systematically sums leading factorially growing terms, thereby stabilizing perturbative convergence and reducing renormalization-scale dependence. We tune charm and bottom quark masses to spin-averaged $1S$ quarkonium states and predict $\Omega_{ccc}$, $\Omega_{ccb}$, $\Omega_{cbb}$, and $\Omega_{bbb}$ baryon masses, as well as QCD-stable baryons containing top quarks. NNLO MRS results undershoot lattice QCD by 125-175 MeV, a difference we attribute to contributions beyond the static perturbative potentials, including $1/m_Q$ corrections. Applying these methods to unequal-mass fully-heavy tetraquarks, we determine the critical heavy-to-light mass ratio for binding and compute binding energies across the mass-ratio landscape.

hep-ph.title: Perturbative Dissipation in Minimal Warm Inflation
hep-ph.author: Daniel J. H. Chung, Nidhi Sudhir, Lian-Tao Wang
hep-ph.abstract: We present an analysis of the perturbative modes of dissipation in the minimal warm inflation model where an axion-inflaton is coupled to a gluon thermal bath through the axion-gauge coupling. The corresponding friction coefficient, which generically is governed by IR physics, for the processes we consider is dominated by Landau damping of soft space-like gluons and the plasmon decay of hard on shell gluons. Since both of these processes are IR dominated, the friction coefficient becomes sensitive to the non-perturbative magnetic mass scale $m_{g}^{-1} \sim (\alpha T)^{-1}$ which in turn leads to the friction coefficient's overall linear proportionality to $\alpha$, which is much less suppressed in $\alpha$ powers compared to the well understood term from Chern-Simons (CS) diffusion $(\propto \alpha^5)$. On the other hand, this contribution to the friction coefficient is suppressed due to slow roll. We show that this can be viewed as a suppression of local spontaneous CPT violation for derivative couplings in general and that time correlations of nonlocal variables which do not fall off at large time separations are what allow an unsuppressed friction coefficient.

hep-ph.title: Probability-based Estimates of the Uncalculated N$^5$LO QCD Contribution to the Hadronic $W$-Boson Decay Width
hep-ph.author: Shu-Heng Yang, Jiang Yan, Xing-Gang Wu, Zhi-Fei Wu
hep-ph.abstract: The perturbative QCD corrections to the hadronic decay width of the $W$ boson are currently known up to next-to-next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order ($\mathrm{N^4LO}$), whereas the exact $\mathrm{N^5LO}$ correction remains unavailable owing to its formidable computational complexity. In this work, we estimate the $\mathrm{N^5LO}$ contributions by adopting Bayesian analysis (BA). Before performing the estimation, the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) is employed to improve the precision of the initial scale-dependent perturbative series. Through recursive application of the renormalization group equation, non-conformal terms are absorbed into the strong running coupling, yielding a scheme-independent, scale-invariant perturbative series with improved convergence. The PMC procedure determines an effective coupling $\alpha_s(Q_*)$, with the PMC scale fixed as $Q_* = 100.102~\mathrm{GeV}$ at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy. Based on the improved and more precise series, the $95.5\%$ BA credible interval yields an uncertainty of $\Delta\delta_\mathrm{QCD}|_{\mathrm{PMC, BA}}^{\mathrm{N^5LO}} = \pm 1.0\times 10^{-5}$. The resulting hadronic branching ratio is $\mathcal{B}(W\to \text{hadrons})|_\mathrm{PMC} = (65.84\pm 1.54)\%$, which is consistent with experimental data within reasonable errors.

hep-ph.title: Heavy flavour production in the presence of a weak magnetic field
hep-ph.author: Sudeep Saha, Sandeep Chatterjee, Ujjal Kumar Dey, Snigdha Ghosh
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate an analytic expression for the cross section, up to order $(eB)^2$, for heavy quark ($Q$) production of mass $m_Q$ through the gluon ($g$) fusion process $g+g \to Q+\bar{Q}$ in the presence of a constant weak external magnetic field $B$ with strength $eB \ll m_Q^2$. This is done using the weak-field expansion of the fermion propagator, calculated with Schwinger's proper-time formalism. Owing to the hierarchy of scales ($m_Q^2 \gg eB$), we neglect the effects of the magnetic field on the quark and antiquark spinors in the external lines. Since the magnetic field breaks rotational invariance, the cross section becomes anisotropic and depends on the orientation angle $\theta$ between the magnetic field and the incoming gluons in the center of mass frame. The lowest-order magnetic correction to the vacuum cross section scales as $(eB)^2$ and has $\cos 2\theta$ and $\cos 4\theta$ dependence, reflecting the breaking of rotational symmetry by the magnetic field. The cross section is maximized when the gluons propagate along the field direction ($\theta = 0, \pi$) and minimized in the perpendicular configuration ($\theta = \pi/2$). The resulting asymmetry peaks near the production threshold and falls with increasing center of mass energy, scaling as $(eB)^2/m_Q^4$ with the quark mass. These results provide direct, calculable signatures of the initial-stage magnetic field in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, which can in principle be imprinted on heavy-flavour observables measured in the final state.

hep-ph.title: Faithful Uncertainties in ML-Based Inverse Problems: GPs, NNs and NTKs for the Triplet PDF
hep-ph.author: Nina Elmer, Sven Krippendorf, Maria Ubiali
hep-ph.abstract: Machine-learning methods are increasingly used to solve inverse problems in physics, where a faithful estimate of the uncertainty on the reconstructed function is as important as its central value. We address this question in the simplest instance of a parton distribution function (PDF) determination: the reconstruction of the non-singlet triplet distribution $T_3(x,Q_0^2)$ from deep-inelastic scattering data. Within a closure-test framework, in which the underlying PDF is known and the pseudo-data carry correlated experimental uncertainties, we compare Gaussian processes with different kernels, neural-network ensembles trained with different loss functions, and empirical neural tangent kernel approximations. We find that methods yielding comparable central reconstructions can produce markedly different uncertainties, and we identify the ingredients that control them: a likelihood that includes the full experimental covariance, the functional prior encoded in the kernel or in the endpoint preprocessing, and, for tangent-kernel approximations, the stage of training at which the kernel is evaluated. A normalised-bias diagnostic shows that calibration depends on the correlations of the predictive covariance, not only on its pointwise width. Our results illustrate why closure tests and covariance-aware diagnostics are essential to validate uncertainties in ML-based approaches to inverse problems.

hep-ph.title: Pure annihilation decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ with improved perturbative QCD formalism
hep-ph.author: Sheng-Yu Wang, Xin Liu, Zhen-Jun Xiao
hep-ph.abstract: We study the pure annihilation decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ for the first time in the standard model with $S$ and $T$ representing the states of the light scalar ($1^3\!P_0$) and tensor ($1^3\!P_2$) correspondingly. Utilizing the assignment $q\bar q$ for light scalars with two-scenarios classification, we calculate the branching ratios of $B_c^+ \to ST$ with the improved perturbative QCD (iPQCD) formalism at leading order in the strong coupling $\alpha_s$. The large branching ratios around $10^{-6}$ within uncertainties in the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa-favored channels, such as $B_c^+ \to a_0(1450) a_2(1320)$, $B_c^+ \to a_0(980, 1450)^+ f_2(1270)$, $B_c^+ \to K_0^*(700, 1430) K_2^*(1430)$, and $B_c^+ \to f_0(500, 1370, 1500) a_2(1320)^+$, are obtained in the iPQCD formalism, which would be tested at the Large Hadron Collider-beauty detector in the (near) future. The relevant tests to these theoretical predictions of large branching ratios associated with typical relative ratios could provide important opportunities for understanding the QCD dynamics of the involved modes or light scalars, as well as for exploring the reliability of the iPQCD formalism. Moreover, the direct charge-parity violating asymmetries in the decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ are naturally zero, since only tree-diagram contributions are involved.

hep-ph.title: Sensitivity of the IceCube atmospheric muon rate to decadal trends in the effective atmospheric temperature
hep-ph.author: Tanvi Krishnan, Gabriela Barenboim, Carlos A. Argüelles
hep-ph.abstract: Decadal changes in the Antarctic stratosphere, generally associated with ozone recovery and shifts in polar circulation, are of broad geophysical interest. However, independent long-term measurements of the atmosphere above the Antarctic interior are scarce. We assess whether the atmospheric muon rate recorded by IceCube could constrain decadal changes in the effective atmospheric temperature, $T_\mathrm{eff}$, a weighted average of temperature through the atmosphere that is most sensitive to the stratosphere. Using public atmospheric reanalysis data and records of cosmic-ray, solar, and geomagnetic variability, we reproduce the measured seasonal response of the IceCube muon rate. We then test whether the same response applies to long-term temperature changes with a different vertical temperature profile. The limiting requirement is detector stability rather than counting statistics: an unmodeled muon rate drift of $1\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$ would mimic a temperature trend of $2.8\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. The long-term rate must therefore be stable to approximately $0.3\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$. Within this budget, snow accumulation contributions can be constrained. For a 14-year record, atmospheric variability gives a one-sided 95% CL statistical sensitivity of $1.6\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. Given this sensitivity, the $\sim0.9,\mathrm{K,decade^{-1}}$ cooling indicated by the 2011-2025 atmospheric records would be constrained at the 95% confidence level after approximately 22 years of measurement.

hep-ph.title: Gravitational form factors of the baryon octet and flavor dependence in an NJL quark--diquark model
hep-ph.author: Yiwei Qiu, Zhibo Liu, Congcong Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate the gravitational form factors $A$, $J$ and $D$ of the baryon octet in a Nambu--Jona-Lasinio quark--diquark model with proper-time regularization. With the diquark poles used for the octet spectrum, the $\Sigma$ has the smallest $|D(0)|$ and the largest $r_D$, $0.675~\mathrm{fm}$ compared with $0.637~\mathrm{fm}$ for the nucleon. Its $A$ radius is smaller than the nucleon's. Along the strange-quark mass trajectory, $r_D^\Sigma-r_D^N$ is negative at the lowest nonzero mass and positive at the other three. The difference $r_A^\Sigma-r_A^N$ is negative at all four masses. At a common spatial resolution, the $\Sigma$ also has the weakest pressure and shear peaks.

hep-ph.title: Towards AI-Agent-Accelerated Research in High-Energy Physics: A Case Study in Monte Carlo Analysis
hep-ph.author: Tianqi Gao, Ruobing Jiang, Dawei Fu, Andrew Michael Levin, Qiang Li, Matthew Kenzie
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate how far contemporary LLM-based agents can participate in multistep computational high-energy-physics research under reproducible human supervision. Using a previously published CEPC Bell-observable analysis in $e^+e^- \to ZH$, $Z \to q\bar q$, $H \to ZZ^* \to 4\mu$ as a case study, we test two capabilities. First, the agent performs an instruction-constrained reproduction: it is explicitly instructed not to use the published numerical results as analysis targets, although no technical information-access barrier is imposed. The analysis definition is fixed before the formal comparison, and the resulting detector-level $I_3$ central values reproduce the four published benchmark points to within about 2% without retuning to those values. Second, the agent is used for an open-ended extension with no target answer supplied. Using 200,000 fast-simulated events, a stage-resolved audit identifies muon isolation as the largest single contribution to the hard-to-detector shift, and subsequent diagnostics connect the effect to angle-dependent isolation efficiency, proximity to the hard $Z \to q\bar q$ system, and mixed electromagnetic activity from muon final-state radiation and hadron decays. Throughout, the agent assists with workflow planning, code and configuration inspection, Monte Carlo production, anomaly diagnosis, control construction, statistical analysis, and result organization, while state-changing actions and final interpretation remain under human control. The study shows that the value of AI agents in HEP may lie not only in faster code generation, but in faster scientific iteration, and motivates systematic benchmarking across historical HEP analyses using correctness, human intervention, and researcher-time efficiency as explicit metrics.

hep-ph.title: Meson spectra in a screened relativized quark model
hep-ph.author: Zhe-Qi Huang, Lei Huang, Xiao-Lei Zhang, Xin-Lei Ge, Hao Chen, Cheng-Qun Pang
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we employed the modified Godfrey--Isgur model to systematically investigate the mass spectra of several light, heavy-light, and heavy-heavy meson systems. In this model, a screened potential is employed to phenomenologically account for modifications to the long-range confining interaction associated with unquenched effects. We performed a global refit of the relevant model parameters to a combined set of 90 adopted meson masses spanning all three sectors, ensuring a consistent parameter determination across the different meson systems. Using the resulting parameter set, we calculated the low-lying and highly excited spectra and the corresponding mixed states in different meson families, and compared our results with existing experimental data and other theoretical results. The assignment of several newly observed structures (such as $B_c^*$ and $D_{s1}(2933)$) have also been discussed based on their predicted masses. Overall, the model describes several main spectroscopic features across different flavors and provides mass predictions for highly excited states that have not yet been experimentally established.

hep-ph.title: Top Spin and CP from Equivariant Transformers
hep-ph.author: Henning Bahl, Marco Menen, Antoine Petitjean, Tilman Plehn
hep-ph.abstract: Measurements of spin correlations and CP are an exciting and challenging part of the precision-LHC program. We first show how L-GATr-slim, as a Lorentz-equivariant transformer, significantly boosts the spin analyzing power for hadronic top quarks. We then show how adding a pseudoscalar channel to its architecture allows us to learn and interpret optimal observables and their CP properties. We demonstrate this for WBF-Higgs production at parton level and top pair production including detector effects.

hep-ph.title: Investigations on the low-lying triply charmed pentaquark states in a constituent quark model
hep-ph.author: Yue-Mei Yin, Chun-Sheng An, Cheng-Rong Deng
hep-ph.abstract: In present work, mass spectrum of the low-lying $cccq\bar{q}$ pentaquarks states with $q\bar{q}=u\bar{u}$, $d\bar{d}$ and $s\bar{s}$, are investigated employing a constituent quark model, within which the spin-dependent hyperfine interactions are taken to be the instanton-induced interaction and the one-gluon-exchange interaction, respectively. The model parameters are fixed by fitting the mass spectrum of the relative $q\bar{q}$ and $qqq$ traditional hadrons. The numerical results show that energies for all the obtained states in the two employed models are higher than corresponding meson-baryon channels, consequently, we roughly estimate strong decays of these states using a simple quark rearrangement model, the corresponding partial width ratios for different decay channels are presented.

hep-ph.title: Extragalactic photon-ALP conversion at CTA energies
hep-ph.author: A. Kartavtsev, G. Raffelt, H. Vogel
hep-ph.abstract: Magnetic fields in extragalactic space between galaxy clusters may induce conversions between photons and axion-like particles (ALPs), thereby shielding the photons from absorption on the extragalactic background light. For TeV gamma rays, the oscillation length ($l_{\rm osc}$) of the photon-ALP system becomes inevitably of the same order as the coherence length of the magnetic field ($l$) and the length over which the field changes significantly (transition length $l_{\rm t}$) due to refraction on background photons. We derive exact statistical evolution equations for the mean and variance of the photon and ALP transfer functions in the non-adiabatic regime ($l_{\rm osc} \sim l \gg l_{\rm t}$). We also make analytical predictions for the transfer functions in the quasi-adiabatic regime ($l_{\rm osc} \ll l, l_{\rm t}$). Our results are important in light of the upcoming Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA), and may also be applied to models with non-zero ALP masses.

hep-ph.title: Matter Spectral Functions from Quantum Gravity
hep-ph.author: Varun Kher, Brandon King, Daniel F. Litim, Manuel Reichert
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate Lorentzian quantum gravity coupled to a template matter sector with gauge fields, scalars and fermions. In the absence of quantised gravity, the matter sector by itself is renormalisable, but UV-incomplete. Provided quantum gravity offers an asymptotically safe UV-completion, we determine the photon and scalar two-point functions in the presence of gravitational fluctuations, and show that both possess a Källén-Lehmann spectral representation. Our results are achieved using functional renormalisation adapted for theories in Lorentzian signature. We explain why and how interactions with gravity modify both the infrared as well as the ultraviolet behaviour of matter spectral functions. We further determine the corresponding form factors on the level of the quantum effective action. Limitations and extensions of our study are discussed alongside implications for particle physics and unitarity of quantum gravity with matter.

hep-ph.title: How Significant are Cosmological Collider Signals in the Planck Data?
hep-ph.author: Petar Suman, Dong-Gang Wang, Wuhyun Sohn, James R. Fergusson, E. P. S. Shellard
hep-ph.abstract: The search for primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) is theoretically well motivated but remains observationally challenging. Tight constraints with low significance for the standard non-Gaussian shapes suggest that detection may lie beyond the reach of near-future experiments. However, tests of PNG are highly template-dependent. From a theory perspective, a whole new family of bispectrum shapes arise in the cosmological collider program, with distinct signatures of heavy particles during inflation. In this work, we provide a class of simplified collider templates for these particles that encompasses a broader range of masses, sound speeds, and interactions. We propose that, given the current state of observations, the most effective strategy to search for PNG signals is through orthogonalizing the collider templates, such that they are uncorrelated with the tightly constrained single field predictions. Our results show that removing the single-field contribution enhances the signal across all four templates studied. Using the {\it Modal} pipeline and \textit{Planck} CMB data, we perform a systematic parameter scan of the (\textit{orthogonalized}) collider templates with the most significant result reaching $2.4\sigma$ for spin-0, after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect; indicative results for spin-1 and spin-2 peak around 2$\sigma$. These results indicate that, with refined collider templates and improved data analysis strategies, there are credible prospects with forthcoming observations to detect PNG {\it and also} identify the presence of massive particles during inflation.

hep-ph.title: New Constraints on Cosmic-ray boosted Sub-GeV Dark Matter via Light Mediators
hep-ph.author: Yang Yu, Guan-Sen Wang, Bo Zhang, Tian-Peng Tang, Bing-Yu Su, Lei Feng
hep-ph.abstract: Traditional direct detection experiments lack the sensitivity to probe the sub-GeV dark matter (DM), primarily due to the low energy of the expected nuclear recoils. In this work, we investigate cosmic-ray (CR) upscattering as a mechanism to accelerate DM particles to detectable velocities in underground experiments. By analyzing four models of DM-nucleon interactions -- namely scalar, vector, pseudoscalar, and axial-vector mediators -- we derive constraints on the coupling parameters using data from the LZ, XENON, and Borexino experiments, covering mediator mass from $10^{-6}$ to $1$ GeV. As the mediator mass varies, the shift in dominance between momentum transfer and mediator mass leads to a turnover in the constraints around $10^{-2}$--$10^{-3}~\mathrm{GeV}$. Our results extend the reach of direct detection into the sub-GeV window and clarify the critical role of momentum dependence in light-mediator scenarios.

hep-ph.title: Challenging the Weak Cosmic Censorship with Phantom Fields
hep-ph.author: Giovanni Caridi, Fabrizio Corelli, Paolo Pani
hep-ph.abstract: Penrose's weak cosmic censorship conjecture asserts that spacetime singularities produced by gravitational collapse are generically hidden behind event horizons, thus preventing them from causally influencing distant observers and preserving the predictability of the exterior region. In this work, we probe this conjecture in a setup that deliberately violates one of its central assumptions - the dominant energy condition - by considering the spherical collapse of a phantom scalar field with negative energy density. In principle, such a field could produce a Schwarzschild geometry with negative mass and therefore no event horizon. Our aim is to assess whether, once the dominant energy condition is abandoned, the fully coupled evolution of matter and geometry can dynamically generate or expose naked singularities, thereby probing the robustness of cosmic censorship. To this end, we perform high-accuracy numerical relativity simulations based on fourth-order finite-difference schemes. Starting from smooth, asymptotically flat initial data representing regular phantom scalar wave packets, we follow their fully nonlinear evolution through collapse or dispersion. While an ordinary (positive-energy) scalar field exhibits the standard Choptuik critical behavior at the threshold of black-hole formation, the phantom field displays qualitatively different dynamics. For all amplitudes considered, we find no evidence for trapped surfaces, naked singularities, or alternative stationary end states. Instead, the phantom scalar field disperses in all the configurations studied. Within the parameter space explored, we find no dynamical violation of cosmic censorship.

hep-ph.title: Rapid and robust simulation-based inference for kilonovae
hep-ph.author: Stephanie M. Brown, Mattia Bulla, Hiranya V. Peiris, Nikhil Sarin, Daniel Mortlock, Stephen Thorp, Gurjeet Jagwani, Stephan Rosswog, Samaya Nissanke
hep-ph.abstract: With the next generation of both electromagnetic and gravitational wave observatories beginning to come online, rapid analysis methods for kilonova data are becoming increasingly important in astronomy. Traditional Bayesian parameter estimation using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is time-consuming and relies on explicit likelihood approximations that can break down when modeling uncertainties are significant. We develop a simulation-based inference (SBI) framework for kilonova parameter estimation using density-estimation likelihood-free inference. The framework uses a Gaussian process emulator trained on $\sim 1300$ POSSIS simulations. We demonstrate that SBI provides a rapid alternative to MCMC that is robust to likelihood misspecification. The standard Gaussian likelihood approximation fails to capture the non-Gaussian, correlated structure of emulator uncertainty; SBI learns this structure directly from forward simulations. Simulation studies show that the SBI method accurately recovers injected parameters, while the MCMC suffers from systematic bias caused by likelihood misspecification. This problem persists when analyzing AT2017gfo, where a subset of the MCMC posteriors pile up at prior boundaries and the SBI posteriors do not. The SBI framework infers a total ejecta mass of $\sim 0.087 M_{\odot}$ dominated by lanthanide-poor ejecta and excludes toroidal and peanut ejecta geometries at the 99th percentile for both components. The SBI framework generates $\sim 2 \times 10^{4}$ posterior samples in seconds.

hep-ph.title: Graviton Floor
hep-ph.author: Himeka Matsuo, Asuka Ito, Kazunori Kohri, Teruaki Suyama, Ryutaro Tomomatsu
hep-ph.abstract: It has been observed that the Universe is permeated by the cosmic photon background, ranging from radio waves to gamma rays. We investigate the conversion of the photon background into gravitons in the presence of background magnetic fields in the Milky Way Galaxy and in blazar jets. We find that the resulting graviton background is dominated by the contribution generated in blazar jets. Importantly, this graviton background constitutes a graviton floor for high-frequency gravitational wave detectors searching for new physics, analogous to the neutrino floor.

hep-ph.title: Cancellation of one-loop time dependence in superhorizon curvature perturbations from all scales
hep-ph.author: Keisuke Inomata
hep-ph.abstract: We show the conservation of the superhorizon curvature perturbations at one-loop level in spatially-flat gauge, including contributions from loop wavenumbers on all scales in the decoupling limit, $\epsilon (\equiv -\dot H/H^2) \to 0$. In contrast to previous works, we do not assume a hierarchy $k \gg q$ between the wavenumber of the loop integral, $k$, and that of the power spectrum, $q$, and we explicitly include the regime $k \lesssim q$. Taking into account the nonlinear relation between the inflaton fluctuation and the curvature perturbation with the $\delta N$ formalism, we show that the apparent time dependence of the one-loop curvature power spectrum cancels once all contributions, including boundary terms, are combined consistently.

hep-ph.title: Spin Femtoscopy: A Framework for Revealing Genuine Spin Correlations
hep-ph.author: Kehao Zhang, Xuan Wang, Xiaofeng Luo
hep-ph.abstract: Spin correlations are among the most fundamental quantum observables in many-body systems, yet they remain difficult to access experimentally in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Existing spin measurements, including hyperon polarization and vector-meson spin alignment, have revealed important single-particle spin phenomena, but genuine two-particle spin correlations in the produced hadronic system remain largely unexplored. Here we propose spin femtoscopy, a framework for accessing genuine two-particle spin correlations through spin-resolved femtoscopic measurements. The key principle is that different two-particle spin configurations can give rise to different femtoscopic correlation functions because of quantum statistics and spin-dependent final-state interactions. Using $\Lambda\Lambda$ pairs as a proof of principle, we exploit the self-analyzing weak decay of $\Lambda$ hyperons to construct spin-sensitive femtoscopic correlation functions with different singlet and triplet admixtures. We show that these observables provide experimental access to the spin-state populations of the pair and allow genuine spin correlations to be separated from spin-dependent femtoscopic mixing caused by quantum statistics and final-state interactions. This work extends femtoscopy from a probe of source geometry and final-state interactions to a framework for revealing the quantum spin structure of strongly interacting matter.

hep-ph.title: Kerr Quasinormal Modes without Variable Separation: A Two-Dimensional Hyperboloidal Teukolsky Solver with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
hep-ph.author: Antonio Ferrer-Sánchez, Daniela D. Doneva, José D. Martín-Guerrero, Stoytcho S. Yazadjiev, Roberto Ruiz de Austri-Bazan, Yolanda Vives-Gilabert, José A. Font
hep-ph.abstract: We use physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to solve the gravitational quasinormal-mode (QNM) eigenvalue problem for Kerr spacetime directly in the two-dimensional hyperboloidal formulation of the Teukolsky equation. This formulation does not require separation of variables and thus retains the coupled radial--angular structure. Such a scheme provides a prototype for calculating the QNMs of beyond-Kerr black holes for which the perturbation equations are non-separable. Sequences with increasing angular momentum are constructed, reaching close to the extremal limit. We focus on the fundamental modes $(\ell,m,n)=(2,0,0)$, $(2,1,0)$, $(2,2,0)$, $(3,3,0)$ and $(4,4,0)$, together with the first two overtones $(2,2,1)$ and $(2,2,2)$. After training, the frequency at every spin is refined by solving the discretized equation for it, so that it depends much less on where the stochastic training happens to stop. Comparison with continued-fraction values shows that every reported real and imaginary frequency component of the production network remains below $0.23\%$ error, with a median deviation of $2\times10^{-4}\%$. For the fundamental modes, both components agree within about $10^{-3}\%$ up to $a/M=0.97$, and the real parts within $5\times10^{-4}\%$ at every spin. Sub-percent accuracy is maintained in the near-extremal regime, where the damping rate becomes small and the modes are longest-lived; there the damping errors grow, and the largest, $0.23\%$, belongs to the $(2,2,1)$ overtone. The results establish a non-spectral numerical route to multidimensional black-hole perturbation eigenproblems which does not match the substantially higher precision of dedicated Kerr solvers but offers greater flexibility and requires less analytical pre-processing. The proposed approach is designed to be applicable to other backgrounds whose perturbation equations do not separate.

hep-ph.title: Dimensional reduction and thermodynamics of a non-local scalar field theory
hep-ph.author: S. Duque Cesar, M. J. Neves
hep-ph.abstract: In this paper, we study the dimensional reduction of a non-local scalar field theory from $1+3$ to $1+2$ dimensions. The bulk theory is governed by an entire-function non-local form factor $e^{-\Box_E/\Lambda^2}$, where $\Lambda$ sets a fundamental high-energy scale. By constraining external classical sources to a bidimensional plane, we perform the exact dimensional reduction, derive the effective planar Green's function in terms of the complementary error function, and propose the corresponding effective non-local pseudo-differential planar Lagrangian. Using the static propagator, we determine the interaction energy between two point-like planar charges, proving that the non-local scale regularizes the short-distance singularity at the origin while smoothly recovering the standard Yukawa potential at long distances. Furthermore, we obtain the retarded, advanced, and Feynman Green's functions in coordinate space, demonstrating that macroscopic causality and tree-level unitarity are preserved. Finally, implementing the Matsubara formalism, we investigate the finite-temperature regime and evaluate the exact thermal free energy, pressure, entropy, and heat capacity. We show that the effective planar theory exhibits a fractional effective number of degrees of freedom ($g_{\rm eff}=1/2$ for $m \ll T \ll \Lambda$, crossing over to $g_{\rm eff}=1$ for $T \gg \Lambda$) originating from kinematic bulk leakage and that pressure, entropy, and heat capacity remain positive at all temperatures.

hep-ph.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe
hep-ph.author: Jintao Zou, Zizhuo Zhao, Yongtao Jia, Ligong Bian
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength ($\alpha$). The effective lifetime of the sound-wave source increases for slower PTs, decreasing for faster PT with larger $\beta/H$ and rising with smaller $\alpha$. While the simulated amplitude of normalized gravitational waves is of order $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2})$, in alignment with Minkowski-spacetime results, the resulting GW spectra differ markedly from those scenarios.

hep-ph.title: Anisotropic spin hydrodynamics in a magnetized medium: entropy-current formulation and minimal linear modes
hep-ph.author: Yiwei Qiu, Duan She, Defu Hou
hep-ph.abstract: We formulate anisotropic relativistic spin hydrodynamics in a parity-even magnetized medium using an Israel--Stewart entropy-current construction. Treating the magnetic field at leading order in the gradient expansion reduces the rotational symmetry to $SO(2)$ and separates spin susceptibilities and dissipative transport into longitudinal, transverse, and mixed channels. A restricted quadratic entropy current yields transient equations for the retained dissipative stresses and spin fluxes. We analyze a minimal linear closure around an unpolarized homogeneous equilibrium. Magnetic-flux perturbations remain dynamical, and spin and magnetic fluctuations mix through the fluid variables without explicit spin-magnetization coupling. Infrared coefficient equations and ultraviolet characteristic expansions organize the magnetosonic and Alfvén-like spectra together with spectator spin-flux poles. The retained first-order boost sectors are unstable already at zero wave number, and the ultraviolet spectrum includes superlinear branches. Positive effective inertias stabilize the zero-momentum gapped modes of the boost sector. For the baseline parameters, finite relaxation times yield asymptotically linear propagation branches and finite relaxation poles, with no growing modes found on the sampled grid. The characteristic speeds depend on the magnetic angle and the spin-transport ratios. We determine their relation to the light cone.

hep-lat.title: Chiral Response of QCD Topology across the Thermal Crossover
hep-lat.author: Heng-Tong Ding, Jin-Biao Gu, José Javier Hernández Hernández, Sheng-Tai Li, Jia Ni
hep-lat.abstract: We introduce a novel relation connecting the light-quark-mass derivative of the topological susceptibility in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) to the connected correlation between the squared topological charge and the integrated light-quark scalar density. This relation gives direct access to the chiral response of QCD topology---the local logarithmic light-quark-mass derivative of the susceptibility---from a single ensemble at fixed quark masses for each temperature, without additional simulations at shifted masses. Applying this relation to $(2+1)$-flavor lattice QCD at $m_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$ over temperatures ranging from well below to well above the chiral crossover, we find that the response rises rapidly through the crossover from approximately unity toward two. This evolution corresponds to a change from nearly linear to nearly quadratic dependence of the topological susceptibility on the light-quark mass. Using the chiral response as the exponent of a local power law in the light-quark mass, we determine its effective amplitude from the topological susceptibility. This amplitude exhibits a maximum near the crossover temperature, reflecting the competition between the decreasing topological susceptibility and the increasing chiral response. These results reveal a thermal reorganization of the quark-mass dependence of QCD topology beyond the suppression of topological fluctuations alone.

hep-lat.title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
hep-lat.author: Gurtej Kanwar, Scott Lawrence, Alessandro Nada, Phiala Shanahan
hep-lat.abstract: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years. This chapter gives an introduction and summary to the use of ML methods to optimize lattice field theory without introducing any uncontrolled approximations. We focus on those directions which are clearly established as of late 2025, marking the 50th anniversary of the beginning of the study of lattice gauge theory. This chapter is a contribution to the online book ``Lattice QCD at 50 years,'' (LQCD@50), edited by Tanmoy Bhattacharya, Maarten Golterman, Rajan Gupta, Laurent Lellouch, and Steve Sharpe.

hep-lat.title: Emergence and polymer physics of the center-vortex network: Confronting SU(4) lattice Yang-Mills theory
hep-lat.author: Luis E. Oxman, Jackson A. Mickley, Derek B. Leinweber
hep-lat.abstract: The geometric organization and statistical properties of center-vortex networks provide a window into the infrared dynamics underlying confinement in Yang-Mills theory. Motivated by this connection, we investigate new consequences of a previously proposed confinement mechanism based on physically equivalent elementary Cartan fluxes. We show that, in the percolating phase, these fluxes dynamically reorganize into center-charge sectors whose dominant vortex tensions satisfy a Casimir scaling law, similar to that observed for confining string tensions. We then confront this result with the first nontrivial Yang-Mills case: the doubly charged vortex chains recently observed in SU(4) lattice simulations. To extract the parameters needed to connect the lattice ensemble with the effective description, we characterize how center-vortex chains grow and bend in SU(3) and SU(4) using polymer-inspired techniques not previously applied to center vortices. We find good quantitative agreement for the SU(4) doubly charged sector, providing further evidence for the proposed mechanism.

hep-lat.title: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
hep-lat.author: Runze Chi, Meng Zeng, Tao Xiang, Yi-Zhuang You, Bertrand I. Halperin, Juven Wang
hep-lat.abstract: Quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall systems is a bulk topological property, typically manifesting on gapless boundaries as spectral flow through chiral edge modes upon flux insertion. When the boundary is anomaly-free, it can be symmetrically gapped by symmetric mass generation (SMG) interactions. However, the effects on quantized charge pumping at an interacting gapped boundary are unclear. We address this using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder quasi-(2+1)d realization of the (1+1)d 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral fermion model with six-fermion interactions at one edge. We find gapless modes near the interacting edge for both weak and strong couplings, but the edge can be in a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling. We also identify spontaneous breaking of the model's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry above a critical interaction strength. Across all three boundary phases, we find quantized charge pumping with the same pumped charge per flux quantum. The spatial distribution of the pumped charge varies between phases. Besides charge pumping, we study how a single injected fermion propagates under open boundary conditions. In the SMG phase, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current develops at the endpoints of the gapped edge, which is absent in the weak- and strong-coupling limits. This current reveals a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to the SMG phase. Additionally, we propose an analogy between charge pumping in this model and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the (3+1)d Standard Model. The anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetries of the 3-4-5-0 model play a role analogous to the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry of the Standard Model. In both settings, charge pumping can be associated with a continuous deformation along a classically defined but quantum-anomalous direction, while a discrete subgroup remains an exact quantum symmetry.

hep-lat.title: Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$ from Chiral Perturbation Theory
hep-lat.author: Alexey Vladimirov
hep-lat.abstract: We construct effective operators for transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions in Chiral Perturbation Theory. The operators constructed from pion and nucleon fields possess the main properties of the QCD operators, including multiplicatively renormalizable rapidity divergences. Extracting the leading rapidity divergence, we find the expression for the Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$ and at the low-energy normalization point, which is model-independent up to an additive constant. In this regime, the Collins-Soper kernel has a nearly constant behavior. We also find that at large $b$ it depends on the isospin channel and on the hadron type, although this dependence is numerically very small.

hep-lat.title: A Machine Learning study of the two-dimensional antiferromagnetic $Q$-state Potts model on the square lattice
hep-lat.author: Shang-Wei Li, Kai-Wei Huang, Chien-Ting Chen, Fu-Jiun Jiang
hep-lat.abstract: The critical phenomena of 2D antiferromagnetic $Q$-state Potts model on the square lattice with $Q=2,3,4,5$ and 6 are investigated using supervised neural networks (NN). Conventional supervised and unsupervised NNs either fail or have difficulty in identifying the correct critical behaviors of these models. Remarkably, despite the fact that the NNs employed here are trained with a particular fixed type training set which contains no information about the considered models (except for $Q=2$), they correctly compute the critical temperatures for the studied physical systems. Particularly, the NN outcomes suggest convincingly that the $Q=3$ model is critical only at zero temperature and $Q=4,5,6$ models remain disordered at all temperatures. Apart from the studied models, our NNs trained with exactly the same training set have successfully determined the critical temperature(s) and the nature of the associated phase transition(s) of another physical system differing dramatically from those considered here. Therefore, our NN has the potential to be a universally applicable NN model in studying phase transitions.

hep-lat.title: Chiral spin symmetry
hep-lat.author: L. Ya. Glozman
hep-lat.abstract: We review the chiral spin symmetry, which is a symmetry of the color charge and of the confining electric part of QCD. Observation of this symmetry in the vacuum upon truncation of the near-zero modes of the Dirac operator implies that the hadron mass in the light quark sector is not due to the quark condensate of the vacuum and that confinement and chiral symmetry breaking are not directly related. Observation of this symmetry above the chiral symmetry restoration crossover suggests that QCD is still in the confining regime with chirally symmetric quarks bound into the color-singlets by the confining electric field. This regime of QCD was called a stringy fluid. At a temperature T_d that is essentially above T_ch the chiral spin symmetry smoothly disappears suggesting that the confining electric field gets screened and one observes a very smooth crossover to the quark-gluon plasma. The three-regimes picture has been further substantiated by the analysis of the N_c scaling of the energy density, the pressure and the entropy density. In the hadron gas they scale as N_c^0, in the stringy fluid as N_c^1 and in the quark-gluon plasma as N_c^2. We have analyzed the fluctuations of conserved charges that scale as N_c^1 above T_ch thus indicating a transition from the hadron gas to the stringy fluid. When N_c gets sufficiently large the three-regimes picture transforms into the three-phases phase diagram. Finally we discuss a confining and chirally symmetric model in 3+1 dimensions. This model demonstrates the chiral symmetry restoration in the confining regime and a delocalization of the color-singlet quark-antiquark systems that become very large at T > T_ch. Consequently the stringy fluid matter is a very dense highly collective system of the overlapping very large color-singlet quark-antiquark "mesons" with a very small mean free path.

hep-lat.title: Framing Anomaly in Lattice Chern-Simons-Maxwell Theory
hep-lat.author: Ze-An Xu, Jing-Yuan Chen
hep-lat.abstract: Framing anomaly is a key property of $(2+1)d$ chiral topological orders, for it reveals that the chirality is an intrinsic bulk property of the system, rather than a property of the boundary between two systems. Understanding framing anomaly in lattice models is particularly interesting, as concrete, solvable lattice models of chiral topological orders are rare. In a previous work, we defined and solved the $U(1)$ Chern-Simons-Maxwell theory on spacetime lattice, showing its chiral edge mode and the associated gravitational anomaly on boundary. In this work, we show its framing anomaly in the absence of boundary, by computing the expectation of a lattice version of the modular $T$ operator in the ground subspace on a spatial torus, from which we extract that $\langle T \rangle$ has a universal phase of $-2\pi/12$ as expected: $-2\pi/8$ from the Gauss-Milgram sum of the topological spins of the ground states, and $2\pi/24$ from the framing anomaly; we can also extract the $2\pi/24$ framing anomaly phase alone from the full spectrum of $T$ in the ground subspace by computing $\langle T^m \rangle$. This pins down the last and most crucial property required for a valid lattice definition of $U(1)$ Chern-Simons theory.

hep-lat.title: Tackling the Sign Problem in the Doped Hubbard Model with Normalizing Flows
hep-lat.author: Dominic Schuh, Lena Funcke, Janik Kreit, Thomas Luu, Simran Singh
hep-lat.abstract: The Hubbard model at finite chemical potential is a cornerstone for understanding doped correlated systems, but simulations are severely limited by the sign problem. In the auxiliary-field formulation, the spin basis mitigates the sign problem, yet severe ergodicity issues have limited its use. We extend recent advances with normalizing flows at half-filling to finite chemical potential by introducing an annealing scheme enabling ergodic sampling. Compared to state-of-the-art hybrid Monte Carlo in the charge basis, our approach accurately reproduces exact diagonalization results while reducing statistical uncertainties by an order of magnitude, opening a new path for simulations of doped correlated systems.

hep-lat.title: Renormalon subtracted nonrelativistic QCD for heavy hadron systems
hep-lat.author: Benoît Assi, Andreas S. Kronfeld, Simon Vaiva, Michael L. Wagman
hep-lat.abstract: We present a renormalon-subtracted formulation of potential nonrelativistic QCD (pNRQCD) for precision spectroscopy of heavy hadron systems, combining variational and Green's function Monte Carlo (VMC/GFMC) methods with static two- and three-body potentials through NNLO in $\alpha_s$ (leading order in $1/m_Q$). Minimal renormalon subtraction (MRS) systematically sums leading factorially growing terms, thereby stabilizing perturbative convergence and reducing renormalization-scale dependence. We tune charm and bottom quark masses to spin-averaged $1S$ quarkonium states and predict $\Omega_{ccc}$, $\Omega_{ccb}$, $\Omega_{cbb}$, and $\Omega_{bbb}$ baryon masses, as well as QCD-stable baryons containing top quarks. NNLO MRS results undershoot lattice QCD by 125-175 MeV, a difference we attribute to contributions beyond the static perturbative potentials, including $1/m_Q$ corrections. Applying these methods to unequal-mass fully-heavy tetraquarks, we determine the critical heavy-to-light mass ratio for binding and compute binding energies across the mass-ratio landscape.

hep-lat.title: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
hep-lat.author: Stephen D.H. Hsu
hep-lat.abstract: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model with gauge and Higgs fields regulated on a finite bosonic lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This retains the familiar continuum treatment of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes. Standard Model anomaly cancellation permits a consistent, gauge-invariant phase for the massless chiral determinant. Yukawa interactions are incorporated with a gauge-covariant spectral cutoff acting on the interaction vertices, not on the fermion propagator. Under the stated analytic conditions, the cutoff can be removed by the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, yielding a finite, exactly gauge-invariant functional integral at fixed bosonic lattice spacing and spacetime volume, including topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At zero Yukawa coupling and on smooth weak-field backgrounds, we establish agreement between the appropriately chirality-matched overlap and continuum Weyl fermion determinants up to local counterterms. We also establish reflection positivity at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta for a modified gauge-field reconstruction; its continuum equivalence with Craig's original reconstruction is not proved. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.

hep-th.title: The Kähler Stability Wall in Perturbative Brane--Antibrane Inflation
hep-th.author: Swapnil Kumar Singh
hep-th.abstract: Perturbative brane--antibrane inflation requires the physical Kähler volume to remain stabilized while the anti-D3 sector supplies the inflationary energy. This paper shows that this requirement imposes an exact analytic boundary on the allowed anti-D3 tension. In the leading nilpotent effective theory, the Kähler minimum and the decompactification barrier disappear through a saddle-node degeneration determined by \(U_\sigma=U_{\sigma\sigma}=0\). The positive-tension branch of this boundary is solved in closed form and uniformized by a single real parameter. The same solution fixes the local scaling of the Kähler mass, barrier height, and canonical distance to the endpoint. Integrating out the volume modulus reveals a Schur-complement singularity, showing that the adiabatic single-field description fails at the same boundary unless the inflaton--volume mixing is suppressed. The result is then translated into necessary flux-arithmetic filters involving the warped throat, D3 tadpole, conifold control, scalar normalization, and the full Kähler-sector mass matrix. Numerical tests verify the critical locus, the saddle-node scaling laws, and the resulting sparse throat-flux filtration. These conditions are necessary for compact realizations; no compact vacuum is asserted without the corresponding global and Wilsonian control checks.

hep-th.title: Explicit Symmetry Breaking in Non-Abelian Scalar Theories and One-Loop Renormalization
hep-th.author: Lucas Ducastelo de C. C. Lima
hep-th.abstract: Non-Abelian gauge theories coupled to scalar fields are fundamental in particle physics, yet they often face high-energy instabilities. In this work, we start by analyzing the classical $SU(2)$ complex scalar model, mapping the scalar multiplet into a real $SO(2N)$ representation to formalize its generalization to $SU(N)$. Within this classical setup, we introduce an explicit gauge symmetry breaking exclusively in the scalar sector by splitting the mass parameters and quartic self-coupling constants. Moving to the quantum level, we employ the background field method and the Schwinger-DeWitt technique to compute the exact one-loop divergences, explicitly demonstrating the renormalizability of the broken theory. Finally, we derive the Renormalization Group equations and analyze the fixed points of the flow. It is shown that this explicit symmetry breaking asymptotically destabilizes the theory, driving the scalar couplings away from the origin and inevitably leading to a Landau pole.

hep-th.title: Andreev reflections and optimal truncation in the unitary Fermi droplet
hep-th.author: Silas R. Beane, Adele Le Borgne, Domenico Orlando, Susanne Reffert, Maximilian Schwick
hep-th.abstract: We study the unitary Fermi gas in an external trap in the double-scaling limit of large flavor number N and large charge Q at fixed Q/N. At leading order, the problem reduces to the spectral zeta function of a BdG operator in an inhomogeneous pairing background. The grand potential admits a gradient expansion with distinct bulk and edge sectors. We show that when the trap is harmonic, the bulk sector expansion terminates: beyond the first three terms every bulk contribution integrates to zero. This cancellation is general and follows from zeros of the Euler beta function computed in the Son-Wingate effective field theory, independent of the low-energy constants. The truncation persists for anisotropic traps in any odd dimension. All higher-order dependence for harmonic potentials is therefore carried by the droplet edge. For anharmonic traps, the asymptotic bulk series is factorially divergent. Using a heat-kernel WKB analysis, we show that its large-order growth, sign oscillations, and optimal truncation are fixed by complex periodic orbits of the BdG problem, which are analytic continuations of Andreev reflections. We numerically confirm the predicted Borel singularities for quartic and sextic traps.

hep-th.title: Discreetly Conformal: Higher-Order Chiral Scalars and the Discrete Series
hep-th.author: Calvin Y.-R. Chen, Kurt Hinterbichler, Samanta Saha, Thomas Yan
hep-th.abstract: With its constant shift symmetry gauged, a massless scalar on two-dimensional flat space defines a conformal field theory whose classical phase space is equivalent to that of a chiral and an anti-chiral Floreanini--Jackiw scalar. We show that this picture generalizes: After gauging a larger set of the shift symmetries of the massless scalar field, it decomposes into a pair of generalized chiral and anti-chiral scalars, described by actions with higher-order spatial derivatives. We spell out their physical and gauge symmetries, and show how these give rise to the hidden conformal symmetry of the scalar with gauged shift symmetries. This lifts to de Sitter space, where we find that the discrete series scalars also decompose into these generalized chiral scalars, providing an explanation for their hidden conformal symmetry.

hep-th.title: Analytic Bounds on Conformal Defect Spectra
hep-th.author: Yuma Furuta, Wataru Harada, Yuya Kusuki, Yin Tang
hep-th.abstract: Conformal defects describe impurities and boundaries at criticality. Their stability depends on the scaling dimensions of operators localized on the defects, but these dimensions are often difficult to determine. We derive analytic upper bounds on the lowest nonvacuum scaling dimension using only two defect entropies and the dimension of a defect-changing operator. The bounds identify when relevant operators must appear on the defect with larger defect entropy. They follow from the conformal bootstrap of four-point functions of defect-changing operators and apply to unitary conformal line defects and to conformal boundaries in two-dimensional CFTs. The Ising and Potts models provide exact checks. In three-dimensional $O(N)$ models, we apply the bounds to direct sums of pinning field defects with symmetry-related orientations. Data from a single such defect exclude stable impurity order with three or more orientations in $O(2)$ and $O(3)$, or four or more in $O(4)$, for any geometry of the orientations, and require a relevant domain-wall operator between individually stable pinning field defects at every nonzero relative angle up to $120^\circ$ in $O(3)$ and up to $109.47^\circ$ in $O(4)$. A direct fuzzy-sphere computation of the lowest domain-wall dimension at different relative angles for $N=2,3,4$ is consistent with these bounds and indicates that, within this class of impurities, only two-state order remains a candidate for stable order in $O(3)$ and $O(4)$, while none survives in $O(2)$. A separate application to AdS/BCFT shows that, at fixed unequal brane tensions, a light boundary-condition-changing operator requires additional light primaries on the boundary with larger boundary entropy.

hep-th.title: Fermionic Kaluza-Klein Reductions
hep-th.author: Francesco Bertucci
hep-th.abstract: We work out the Kaluza--Klein (KK) compactification on a general product spacetime for free spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 fields in arbitrary dimension. The analysis is performed at the level of the action, and the resulting lower-dimensional theory describes infinite towers of massive particles whose masses are related to the eigenvalues of the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators on the internal space. A Hodge-like decomposition is used to write down a KK ansatz for spin-3/2 fields, and the fate of gauge invariance is discussed.

hep-th.title: AdS to dS Flows Dual to Pseudo-Hermitian Theories
hep-th.author: José M. Begines, Antón F. Faedo, Carlos Hoyos, Daniele Musso
hep-th.abstract: We construct generalizations of ''centaur" geometries in more than two dimensions as solutions of Einstein gravity coupled to a ghost scalar. The solutions interpolate between asymptotically anti-de Sitter and asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes, with the two asymptotic regions separated by a horizon. A holographic interpretation is that they are dual to pseudo-Hermitian theories obtained from the continuation of real couplings and operators to purely imaginary values. One family of solutions is obtained from a supergravity theory that is a consistent truncation with a known embedding in string theory. We study the thermodynamic and linear stability of the solutions, and determine the uplift of the supergravity solutions to eleven dimensions.

hep-th.title: Density kernel and temporal quantum information probes in double-scaled SYK
hep-th.author: Johanna Erdmenger, Maximilian Gaschler, Jonathan Karl, Arnab Kundu, Georg Setzer
hep-th.abstract: Entanglement is conventionally defined through a Hilbert space bipartition on a fixed time slice. Recent work has generalized this notion to multiple times through a non-Hermitian density kernel constructed from temporal correlation functions, encoding causal response, temporal non-classicality and quantum dynamics. We construct this kernel in the double-scaled Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (DSSYK) model using its exact chord Hilbert space formulation and study the resulting temporal information diagnostics. The direct sum structure of chord space naturally introduces a coarse-graining under which coherence between different chord sectors is removed. We show that the corresponding kernel measures quantify how information is dynamically transferred across subregions in the chord Hilbert space. We find that decreasing $\lambda$ enhances the propagation of temporal correlation across chord sectors, as well as the loss of memory within a fixed sector. This accelerated temporal dynamics in the small $\lambda$ limit coincides with the emergence of a semiclassical gravity description. Depending on the chord space partition, the probes exhibit either saturation, a growth followed by a decay, or temporary memory loss. The characteristic propagation time is nicely captured by a wavefront picture in Krylov space, with position-dependent hopping parameters that are determined by the DSSYK Lanczos coefficients. Finally, given the quantum sine-dilaton gravity description of DSSYK and its connections to de Sitter holography, our results provide a controlled setting for probing temporal quantum correlations across quantum and semiclassical gravitational regimes, and motivate a geometric interpretation of the density kernel.

hep-th.title: Reflecting Baths and Black Hole Interior Islands in JT Gravity
hep-th.author: Dmitry S. Ageev, Anastasia N. Zueva
hep-th.abstract: We study the evolution of entanglement entropy within the island prescription in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to finite non-gravitating baths bounded by reflecting walls. For free massless Dirac matter, we study the evolution of entanglement entropy, explicitly accounting for correlations induced by the reflecting boundaries. For sufficiently short baths, the no-island entropy saturates below the thermodynamic black hole entropy, avoiding the usual information paradox associated with its unbounded growth. For larger baths, reflected correlations drive the exterior quantum extremal surface toward the future horizon, leading to a temporary disappearance of the the near-horizon exterior island branch. We find that this branch first appears at a scrambling-like scale, and it reappears at a time that is proportional to the size of the bath. We extend the extremization across the horizon using regular Kruskal coordinates and identify real quantum extremal surfaces in the black hole interior. We show that, in the parameter regime studied, interior island configurations provide the dominant contribution to the radiation entropy during the exterior disappearance time interval, resolving the reappearance of the information paradox in an exterior-only description.

hep-th.title: A Song of Spice and Ice: A diagonal dual to dS$_3$ & its Galilean flat space limit
hep-th.author: Arjun Bagchi, Sharang Rajesh Iyer, K. Narayan
hep-th.abstract: We propose a diagonal CFT dual to asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes in three dimensions (3d), constructed from the holomorphic part of the CFT dual at the future boundary and the antiholomorphic part of the CFT dual at the past boundary, in part inspired by an antipodal map between the two CFT copies. This gives equal and opposite imaginary central charges for the holomorphic and antiholomorphic sectors. The corresponding diagonal holographic energy-momentum tensor expectation values are constructed from the Wavefunction at the future boundary and its conjugate. This enables a recovery of the entropy of $dS_3$, as well as a family of complex Kerr $dS_3$ spacetimes with two real horizons, by a Cardy formula.We then explore the flatspace limit of our dS construction. With the central charges as above, the flatspace limit naturally induces a Galilean contraction on the dual diagonal 2d CFT, in contrast to the more familiar Carrollian limit when 3d Asymptotically Flat Spacetime (AFS) is approached from $AdS_3$. The corresponding limit for the complex Kerr family above leaves the inner horizon intact, resulting in flat space complex black holes ($\mathbb{C}$BH) that are closely related to flat space cosmologies which arise from BTZ black holes in AdS$_3$. We recover the entropy of these $\mathbb{C}$BHs by the BMS-Cardy formula.

hep-th.title: Dressed AdS$_4$ black holes in M-theory from the 3d superconformal index
hep-th.author: Evan Deddo, Seppe Geukens, Leopoldo A. Pando Zayas, Christoph F. Uhlemann, Wenjie Zhou
hep-th.abstract: The superconformal index of 4d $\mathcal N\,{=}\,4$ SYM has been shown to exhibit a rich phase structure, whose holographic interpretation in AdS$_5$ involves (dual-)dressed black holes, gray galaxies, and graviton gas contributions. Here we extend the analysis to 3d CFTs, focusing on ABJM theory and the $\mathcal N=4$ ADHM theory. We study the microcanonical superconformal index with two independent charges at finite $N$ and obtain exact signed state degeneracies up to large charges. The results exhibit the black hole physics expected to emerge at large-$N$, including isolated black holes and black holes dressed by additional matter.

hep-th.title: NLO corrections to charged-current correlators near extremality: non-Abelian hydrodynamics meets AdS$_2$
hep-th.author: Matti Järvinen, Elias Kiritsis, Francesco Nitti, Andrea Olzi, Edwan Préau
hep-th.abstract: We analytically compute the longitudinal charged-current correlator in a near-extremal holographic plasma with quark and isospin chemical potentials, $\mu_q$ and $\mu_3$ respectively. To this end, we study fluctuations of gauge fields around a low-temperature AdS$_5$ Reissner-Nordström black hole charged both under the quark number and the isospin. The result is obtained at next-to-leading order in a hydrodynamic expansion where apart from the temperature and isospin chemical potential, the frequency and momenta are small compared to the quark chemical potential, $\omega,k,T,\mu_3\ll\mu_q$. This approach captures the interplay between the hydrodynamic-like pole and the tower of infrared modes produced by the AdS$_2$ throat controlling the geometry of the black hole near extremality. At zero isospin chemical potential, the resulting quasinormal-mode formula reproduces the collision of the diffusive pole with the infrared spectrum, while the finite isospin chemical potential lifts this collision. The analytic spectrum agrees precisely with the full numerical results. The next-to-leading-order correlator also substantially improves the spectral function beyond the standard hydrodynamic regime $\omega,k,\mu_3\ll T$, extending the agreement with numerics to larger frequencies and momenta.

hep-th.title: Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
hep-th.author: Euihun Joung, J. A. Rosabal
hep-th.abstract: We formulate the scalar and form-field sector of type IIB supergravity as an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary. Unlike the pseudo-action, it is a genuine action principle with manifest global $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry. The IIB fields arise as edge modes: a boundary term breaks the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, so the axion-dilaton parametrizes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(2)$, and the boundary field equations give the duality relations, including $F_5$ self-duality. As the action never refers to the axion-dilaton directly, S-duality monodromies become holonomies of a flat connection.

hep-th.title: Simplicity of the three-point stress-tensor form factor beyond the planar limit
hep-th.author: Song He
hep-th.abstract: We express the complete three-loop subleading-color finite remainder of the three-point stress-tensor-multiplet form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory as a permutation sum of a single $A_2$-type function. The non-product part of the seed is a combination of 35 weight-six generalized polylogarithms, while all lower-weight products and zeta-value terms belong to the same five-letter algebra. A bootstrap based on independently computed collinear data, branch-cut constraints and empirical final-entry relations determines both the symbol and the full function. The remaining function-level ambiguity is proportional to $\zeta_2$ times the two-loop planar remainder and is fixed by a single final-entry relation. The weight-three left coproduct factors of the planar and subleading-color results span the same space modulo products; at weight four, the subleading-color result contains four additional nonclassical directions. Through the established maximal-transcendentality correspondence, this compact representation also describes the weight-six subleading-color sector of Higgs-plus-three-gluon amplitudes in QCD. We also construct a four-loop candidate symbol space under a conjectural extension of the three-loop constraints.

hep-th.title: AdS${}_3$/BCFT${}_2$ correspondence and 't Hooft anomaly of U(1) symmetry
hep-th.author: Hikaru Toya, Satoshi Yamaguchi
hep-th.abstract: We investigate how a U(1) 't Hooft anomaly obstructs symmetry-preserving boundary conditions from the perspective of the AdS${}_3$/BCFT${}_2$ correspondence. By considering a U(1) Maxwell--Chern--Simons system in the bulk spacetime, we show that the BCFT current is not conserved at the boundary. We also derive the general solution for the gauge field in AdS${}_2$ slicing.

hep-th.title: Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space
hep-th.author: Albert Schwarz
hep-th.abstract: The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer frominfrared divergences

hep-th.title: Analogue Schwinger Pair Production in Acoustic Black Holes
hep-th.author: Ruo-Han Wang, Yu-Ye Cheng, Jia-Rui Sun
hep-th.abstract: We show that an analogue Schwinger pair production can be realized in Reissner-Nordstr{ö}m-like acoustic black holes constructed from a Bose-Einstein condensate subject to a synthetic vector potential.
